\chapter{Hungry, Thirsty, Sleepy}
\label{ch:hi-hungry-thirsty-sleepy}
\hlchaptermodality{124}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say I am hungry, thirsty or sleepy, that I am sweating, and that I have a headache.}

Complete HI-C124-sirdard: say what the body needs.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[bhūkhā]{\hi{भूखा} (bhūkhā) — hungry}

\label{lesson:HI-C124-bhukha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for what's going on, then the Hindi for have you eaten.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{भूखा}}
\textbf{\hi{भूखा}} (\emph{bhūkhā}) — \textquotedblleft{}hungry\textquotedblright{}. A woman says \textbf{\hi{भूखी}}.

It is \textbf{\hi{भूख}}, \textquotedblleft{}hunger\textquotedblright{}, made into a description. \textbf{\hi{मैं} \hi{भूखा} \hi{हूँ}} — \textquotedblleft{}I am hungry\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Hunger, made into how you are.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhūkhā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhūkhā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{maiṁ bhūkhā hūṁ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for what's going on, then the Hindi for have you eaten, then say \emph{bhūkhā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{भूखा} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Hungry\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[pyāsā]{\hi{प्यासा} (pyāsā) — thirsty}

\label{lesson:HI-C124-pyasa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for have you eaten, then the Hindi for hungry.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{प्यासा}}
\textbf{\hi{प्यासा}} (\emph{pyāsā}) — \textquotedblleft{}thirsty\textquotedblright{}. A woman says \textbf{\hi{प्यासी}}.

The same move: \textbf{\hi{प्यास}}, \textquotedblleft{}thirst\textquotedblright{}, becomes \textbf{\hi{प्यासा}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Thirst, made into how you are.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pyāsā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pyāsā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{maiṁ pyāsā hūṁ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for have you eaten, then the Hindi for hungry, then say \emph{pyāsā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{प्यासा} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Thirsty\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[nīnd ā rahī hai]{\hi{नींद} \hi{आ} \hi{रही} \hi{है} (nīnd ā rahī hai) — I'm sleepy}

\label{lesson:HI-C124-nindaa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for hungry, then the Hindi for thirsty.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{नींद} \hi{आ} \hi{रही} \hi{है}}
\textbf{\hi{नींद} \hi{आ} \hi{रही} \hi{है}} (\emph{nīnd ā rahī hai}) — \textquotedblleft{}I'm sleepy\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}sleep is coming\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{नींद}} is the sleep you know. Sleep \emph{comes} to you, the way anger and laughter do.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Sleep, which comes to you.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nīnd ā rahī hai}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nīnd ā rahī hai}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{mujhe nīnd ā rahī hai}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for hungry, then the Hindi for thirsty, then say \emph{nīnd ā rahī hai} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{नींद} \hi{आ} \hi{रही} \hi{है} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}I'm sleepy\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[pasīnā]{\hi{पसीना} (pasīnā) — sweat}

\label{lesson:HI-C124-pasina}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for thirsty, then the Hindi for I'm sleepy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{पसीना}}
\textbf{\hi{पसीना}} (\emph{pasīnā}) — \textquotedblleft{}sweat\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{बहुत} \hi{पसीना} \hi{आ} \hi{रहा} \hi{है}} — \textquotedblleft{}I'm sweating a lot\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}a lot of sweat is coming\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Sweat, in the coming frame.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pasīnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pasīnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{bahut pasīnā ā rahā hai}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for thirsty, then the Hindi for I'm sleepy, then say \emph{pasīnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{पसीना} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Sweat\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[sirdard]{\hi{सिरदर्द} (sirdard) — a headache}

\label{lesson:HI-C124-sirdard}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for I'm sleepy, then the Hindi for sweat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{सिरदर्द}}
\textbf{\hi{सिरदर्द}} (\emph{sirdard}) — \textquotedblleft{}a headache\textquotedblright{}.

It is \textbf{\hi{सिर}}, \textquotedblleft{}head\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\hi{दर्द}}, \textquotedblleft{}pain\textquotedblright{}, both yours already. \textbf{\hi{मुझे} \hi{सिरदर्द} \hi{है}} — \textquotedblleft{}I have a headache\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Hungry, thirsty, sleepy, sweat, and a headache.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sirdard}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sirdard}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{mujhe sirdard hai}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for I'm sleepy, then the Hindi for sweat, then say \emph{sirdard} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{सिरदर्द} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A headache\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
